issues.failure_explanation: The weak condition only gives growth like α^2 r^2 and r^2/α^2. Take T(x)=αx, which is weakly α-bi-Lipschitz. The claimed lower bound α^2 r^2 ≥ α(1-γ) r^2 then fails whenever α<1-γ. Similarly, T(x)=x/α violates the upper bound (1/α+γ) r^2 for small α, e.g. α=1/2. Both counterexamples work on separated pairs if M has large enough diameter. No proof is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with constants α^2(1-γ) and (1+γ)/α^2 and threshold (1-α^2)/(α^2γ); both inequalities then follow by direct algebra.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bi-Lipschitz constants for well-separated pairs are false, and so is the prose that relies on this implication.
issues.title: Weak-to-strong bi-Lipschitz proposition has false constants
